entries.title: Leviticus 13:2
segments: Leprosy; a foul disease covering the body with a kind of white scales; from its loathsome and incurable character, it is often referred to as an emblem of sin.  The terms, "a rising, a scab, or bright spot," describe three different varieties in its form of appearing.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:3
segments:
Unclean; leprous, and therefore to be excluded from divine ordinances and from society. 
 
Sin occasions a great variety of diseases, and will finally consign the body to the grave, and the soul, unless cleansed from its pollution, to perdition.  All should therefore be solicitous to know whether they are under its power; and if so, to apply without delay to Him who can say with effect, I will; be thou clean.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:6
segments: Dark; or pale, dim, in opposition to bright.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:7
segments: In doubtful cases, persons should not be hasty in deciding upon their own spiritual state.  They should obtain all the light they can from experienced ministers and Christians; from self-examination, from the Scriptures, and religious books.  Above all, they should go habitually to God, earnestly praying, Search me, O God, and know my heart; try me, and know my thoughts; and see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:9
segments: The plague of leprosy; another variety in its form, namely, the rising,

entries.title: Leviticus 13:11
segments: Old habits of sin, unless they are effectually renounced and forsaken, will revive and break out at times into flagrant transgression, and the last state of a man be worse than the first.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:13
segments: He is clean; either it is not a true leprosy, or the leprosy has in this way healed itself.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:17
segments: Ministers of the gospel, and those who are called not only to judge of their own state, but to give directions to others, need great wisdom. They should be familiar with the Scriptures, well acquainted with themselves, and accustomed in every thing, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, to make known their requests unto God.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:24
segments:
A hot burning; in the original, a burning of fire; which seems ot mean a sore made by fire in which the plague of leprosy appears.  Some, however, suppose that it is an inflamed sore. 
 
  And the quick flesh that burneth have; or, "and the mark of the burning be," that is, break out into.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:28
segments: Not every sin of which a man may have been guilty, of itself merely, proves him to be in an unregenerate state; while no transgression of God's law, known, allowed, and persevered in, or not repented of and forsaken, can consist with a gracious and safe state.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:30
segments: Beard; a disease in the part from which the beard grows, and affecting the beard itself.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:31
segments: There is no black hair in it; the presence of this would be a favorable sign,
.  Its absence makes the case doubtful.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:39
segments: Darkish white; or dullish white, in opposition to bright white spots.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:44
segments: Persons may be free from one kind of sin, and yet deeply involved in another; and we are not to conclude that we are not under condemnation because we are not guilty of all sorts of transgressions, of sins which others practise, or which are known to our fellow-men; but we are to search out and forsake all iniquity; crying unto God, Cleanse thou me from secret faults, as well as, Keep me back from presumptuous transgressions.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:45
segments: A covering upon his upper lip; this was a sign of mourning and humiliation.
Unclean, unclean; as a warning to others not to approach him.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:46
segments: Sin is contagious, and all suitable efforts should be made to prevent one wicked person from corrupting others; we should not have for our companions any who lead us into sin.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:47
segments: The plague of leprosy; some infection that had a general resemblance to leprosy.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:51
segments: A fretting leprosy; corroding and destroying the cloth.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:55
segments:
Bare; deprived of its nap. 
 
  Within or without; on the inner or outer side of the garment.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:56
segments: Out of the warp, or out of the woof; as neither the warp nor the woof could be removed separately, the meaning seems to be, that by rending out the part affected, he shall remove the leprosy, whether it have its seat in the warp or the woof.

entries.title: Leviticus 13:57
segments: We should avoid not only the commission of sin, but the occasions of it; and make whatever sacrifice is needful to be delivered from its power.
